Our Product and Engineering organisation is structured into four tribes: Custody, Accounts, Experience, and Cloud & Security. Each tribe contains multiple autonomous squads, with clear full ownership over specific product domains.
The squads are intentionally small and cross-functional, typically made up of an Engineering Manager, Product Manager, and 3–5 engineers with complementary skills aligned to the domain they own.
We operate in a build-and-run model, with teams responsible for the full software lifecycle, from architecture and delivery through to operational support and incident management.
Our core platform is built on AWS serverless technologies including Lambda, SQS, EventBridge, API Gateway, S3, and ECS. We primarily develop in TypeScript and Node.js, with MongoDB as our primary document database. We also have a small number of C# services and are continuing to evolve our platform architecture, including expanding our use of ECS Fargate.
Infrastructure is managed through a combination of Terraform and Serverless Framework. We use GitHub Actions for CI/CD and incident.io to support our incident management processes and operational workflows.
We care deeply about engineering quality, pragmatic architecture, and continuous improvement. If you’d like to go deeper, we’re happy to share more about our engineering practices and technology radar during the interview process.

About Pantheon
Pantheon WebOps Platform powers the open web, running more than 300,000 sites in the cloud for customers including Google, Princeton, Salesloft and Doctors Without Borders. Every day, thousands of developers and marketers create, iterate, and scale WordPress and Drupal sites to reach billions of people globally.

Pantheon ’s multitenant, container-based platform enables organizations to manage all of their websites from a single dashboard. Organizations including Clorox and the United Nations drive results through accelerated development and real-time publishing using Pantheon ’s collaborative workflows.

The Data Platform team powers Pantheon ’s data infrastructure and delivers analytics across the company. We’ve built a robust, configuration-driven data platform that handles extraction, ingestion, curation, compliance, security, and enterprise-wide access to data — and we’re looking for a Staff Software Engineer to take it to the next level.
In this role, you’ll extend the platform beyond its current foundation to surface data insights directly within our Product experience, and to power the infrastructure behind Machine Learning and LLM-driven insights.

As the lead technical member of the Data Platform team, you’ll architect the next generation of services that let every team at Pantheon trust and act on data, working closely with Software Engineers, Data Engineers, Analytic Engineers and Product.

The platform runs on Python, Airflow, Kubernetes, configuration YAML, Great Expectations, and Terraform.
Pantheon ’s core values are Trust, Teamwork, Passion, and Customers First. Within engineering, we value collaboration, character, autonomy, and a no-blame culture — and we’re active participants in several open-source communities.

Take the platform to the next level. Extend our robust, configuration-driven data platform to surface data insights directly within the Product experience, and to power the infrastructure behind Machine Learning and LLM-driven insights.
Enhance platform architecture. Serve as the lead technical member of the Data Platform team, maintaining and enhancing our core platform services: Ingest as a Service (consistent extraction and loading into the data lake), Curation as a Service (configuration-driven, audited transformations) and Retention as a Service (historical data hosting that balances access, compliance, and cost).
Build with modern data infrastructure. Work hands-on with Snowflake (including Snowpark for Python), Google Cloud Platform, Airflow , Docker, and Terraform.
Mentor the team. Guide a team of engineers in designing and implementing high impact projects, raising the technical bar across the group.
Own the full lifecycle. Operate in a full DevOps model — development, testing, operations, and support for the systems you build.
Raise the bar. Drive continuous improvement of engineering standards for coding, testing, deployment, and communication.
Partner cross-functionally. Work with Product, Sales, Ops, Finance and other teams to deliver high-impact data solutions and support a self-service, data-driven culture across Pantheon .
Support reliability. Participate in the Data team’s on-call rotation, contributing to the stability, reliability, and performance of Pantheon ’s data infrastructure.
What You Will Need to Succeed
Distributed data systems: deep understanding of processing large-scale datasets across distributed systems, with a clear grasp of the trade-offs in designing for high throughput and low latency.
Data modeling and architecture: ability to design, implement, and optimize scalable data models (dimensional, normalized) for both OLAP and OLTP systems, ensuring data integrity and query performance.
Data governance & observability: experience with data governance frameworks, data catalogs, and observability tooling that keep large-scale data assets discoverable, trusted, and compliant.
Technical leadership: experience setting technical direction for a platform or team, translating ambiguous requirements into clear architecture, and mentoring other engineers.
Customer/product focus: an understanding of the direct and indirect business value of your work, ensuring data solutions align with company-wide goals and deliver impact for internal and external customers.
Communication: the ability to clearly articulate technical designs, project status, and risk to both technical peers and non-technical stakeholders, while remaining open to others’ ideas.
Quality mindset: experience embedding automated test coverage, data validation, and idempotent design into deployment pipelines.
Design principles: security, trust, and dependability are foundational to how you build — declarative design, modularity, containers, and idempotency should genuinely excite you.

AI2IO helps organizations navigate the complex landscape of technology solutions, from foundational IT services and system support to advanced software integration, automation, and cutting-edge AI implementations. Our expertise spans IT infrastructure management, custom software development, seamless system integrations, and optimization of low-code business automation, empowering clients to maximize their existing technology investments.
Join us and be part of a team where your voice matters, your work makes an impact, and your growth is a shared priority.
Position Title
Software Engineer Technical Lead
Position Location
Remote - work virtually from anywhere in the United States

ai2io is seeking a Software Engineer Technical Lead with deep C#/.NET, Microsoft Azure, and ASP.NET Blazor experience to own the technical direction and engineering outcomes of a software team. Blazor is our strategic web-application platform. You will remain a hands-on contributor while guiding architecture, delivery, production readiness, secure engineering, and team capability across our Microsoft-centric stack.
The current application portfolio also includes React applications that ai2io must responsibly maintain while planning and executing their transition to C#/.NET and Blazor.

Strong React and TypeScript experience is therefore important for sustaining business continuity, stabilizing inherited applications, understanding their behavior and dependencies, and leading deliberate migrations without disrupting users or critical workflows. This role is not intended to establish React as a long-term parallel platform.
Experience with Revit, electrical or mechanical engineering, BIM, MEP workflows, or the broader architecture, engineering, and construction industry is valuable because many ai2io products support specialized engineering work, but that domain experience is not required.
Essential Functions
This role combines hands-on leadership of the strategic .NET and Blazor platform with accountable stewardship of transitional React applications, including their reliable operation and planned conversion.
Own Technical Direction for the Strategic Platform
Serve as the team's primary technical decision-maker for solutions built with C#/.NET, ASP.NET Blazor, Microsoft Azure, SQL Server, Microsoft Graph API, Entra ID, and related Microsoft technologies.
Lead design for new features and systems and guide teams toward C#/.NET and Blazor for ongoing development unless an approved exception is warranted.
Produce durable architecture decision records, system diagrams, API contracts, migration guidance, and implementation plans that engineers can execute against.
Define and enforce coding standards, pull-request practices, definition of done, automated testing expectations, accessibility, documentation, and the engineering quality bar.
Remain hands-on in production C#, Blazor, Azure, and targeted React/TypeScript work where continuity, diagnosis, or migration risk requires direct contribution.
Maintain Transitional React Applications
Own the technical health of React applications while ai2io is responsible for their continued operation, including defect resolution, dependency updates, security findings, diagnostics, testing, and production support.
Quickly assess inherited React applications, documenting architecture, build and deployment processes, dependencies, data flows, integrations, ownership gaps, operational risks, and critical business workflows.
Prioritize stabilization work that protects users and business continuity without expanding avoidable long-term investment in the transitional React platform.
Establish sufficient React and TypeScript coding, testing, review, and release practices to maintain inherited applications safely through their remaining lifecycle.
Identify unsupported, fragile, or high-risk components early and present clear mitigation and migration options.
Lead React-to-Blazor Conversion
Create phased migration strategies that move React applications and workflows to C#/.NET and Blazor while preserving user outcomes, data integrity, integrations, and operational continuity.
Decide what should be migrated, redesigned, consolidated, retired, or temporarily retained based on business value, technical risk, maintainability, usage, and migration cost.
Decompose migrations into controlled increments with coexistence boundaries, interface contracts, acceptance criteria, rollback plans, and explicit cutover checkpoints.
Partner with Product Owners, business stakeholders, and users to validate functional parity and identify where migration is an opportunity to simplify or improve the experience rather than reproduce unnecessary complexity.
Retire superseded React components and dependencies after verified cutover, ensuring documentation, monitoring, support ownership, and source repositories reflect the final state.
Plan and Coordinate Technical Delivery
Break complex features and migrations into coherent increments, identifying technical discovery, dependencies, sequencing constraints, integration risks, and milestones before commitments are finalized.
Own technical feasibility, decomposition, estimates, dependencies, execution health, and technical risk behind team commitments; partner with the Project Manager on the integrated schedule, stakeholder communication, scope coordination, and overall delivery process.
Coordinate engineers through purposeful delegation, design checkpoints, code review, blocker removal, and clear implementation direction.
Communicate business-continuity and migration tradeoffs clearly, bringing evidence and recommended options rather than status alone.
Own Azure Production Readiness
Own team-level readiness for Azure-hosted releases, including deployment planning, observability, diagnostics, rollback considerations, support documentation, and resolution of material technical risks.
Guide appropriate use of Azure application, data, identity, integration, storage, secrets, and monitoring services in alignment with organizational standards.
Lead investigation of significant production issues across Blazor and transitional React applications, coordinating mitigation, root-cause analysis, and follow-up improvements.
Convert incidents, support trends, recurring defects, and performance evidence into prioritized reliability, testability, migration, and maintainability work.
Set the Secure Engineering and Quality Bar
Ensure implementations follow approved practices for authentication, authorization, secrets, data access, dependency management, input validation, privacy, and secure coding.
Own testing strategy across .NET unit and integration tests, Blazor component and end-to-end tests, and sufficient React test coverage to support maintenance and migration confidence.
Ensure CI/CD pipelines apply reliable automated quality gates and provide actionable feedback for both strategic and transitional applications.
Balance feature delivery and business continuity with deliberate management of technical debt, security findings, migration risk, and long-term platform simplification.

Nebius is leading a new era in cloud infrastructure for the global AI economy. We are building a full-stack AI cloud platform that supports developers and enterprises from data and model training through to production deployment, without the cost and complexity of building large in-house AI/ML infrastructure.
Built by engineers, for engineers. From large-scale GPU orchestration to inference optimization, we own the hard problems across compute, storage, networking and applied AI.
Listed on Nasdaq (NBIS) and headquartered in Amsterdam, we have a global footprint with R&D hubs across Europe, the UK, North America and Israel. Our team of 1,500+ includes hundreds of engineers with deep expertise across hardware, software and AI R&D.
About the Product
Token Factory is focused on building a next-generation platform that enables companies to seamlessly integrate AI into their products and workflows. Our vision is to create a powerful, open, and scalable alternative for deploying and managing AI systems—making advanced AI infrastructure more accessible to both fast-growing startups and large enterprises.
We work with a wide range of customers, from AI-first companies to established technology organisations, helping them run AI workloads reliably at scale. Our goal is to become a leading platform for high-performance AI inference, delivering predictable latency, strong reliability, and the ability to scale to meet demanding production needs.
Customer feedback plays a central role in how we build—our development process is highly iterative and closely aligned with real-world use cases.

The Models Team is responsible for onboarding state-of-the-art (SOTA) open-source models into Nebius TokenFactory, including models such as DeepSeek V4 Pro, GLM 5.1, Kimi K2.6, and Minimax M2.7. A major focus of the team is serving large-scale AI models efficiently and reliably in production.
To achieve this, we work on advanced inference and systems optimization techniques, including:
Cache-aware routing
NUMA-aware deployments
KV-cache offloading
Disaggregated serving architectures
Autoscaling with high-speed model loading over InfiniBand / RoCE
The team maintains and extends forks of leading inference frameworks such as vLLM and TRT-LLM . We have deep expertise in production-scale model serving and regularly support the Solutions Architects team on the most demanding customer PoCs.
To operate efficiently at scale, we invest heavily in tooling and automation.

Performance, quality, and smoke-testing frameworks
Hyperparameter optimization for inference framework configurations
Gibberish detection systems
Automated rollout pipelines for inference framework upgrades
Diagnostics and observability tooling
Traffic replay systems
Automated search for optimal serverless deployment configurations
We collaborate closely with model builders, open-source communities, Nebius Cloud teams, and hardware vendors to continuously improve our serving infrastructure.
The team is highly goal-oriented and outcome-driven, with a strong focus on delivering results rather than following rigid processes.
Team Structure
We are currently a team of eight engineers distributed across Europe, with members based in the Netherlands, the United Kingdom, Germany, and Latvia.
Our workflows are optimized for remote collaboration. At the same time, we meet in person every one to two months at one of our locations to work together, brainstorm new ideas, and plan upcoming milestones.
While many team members joined without extensive AI/ML experience, we have rapidly developed strong expertise in large-scale model serving and AI infrastructure.
Technology
Our work is deeply integrated with the broader cloud and infrastructure ecosystem. We primarily use Go and Python to build and scale backend systems. We collaborate closely with teams working on cloud infrastructure, observability, reliability, fault tolerance, and platform engineering. The challenges we solve sit at the intersection of distributed systems, high-performance computing, and modern AI infrastructure.

Experience serving LLMs in production
Strong Python and/or Go programming skills
Experience designing and operating highly scalable, highly available distributed services

Contributions to vLLM, SGLang, TRT-LLM, or NVIDIA ecosystem open-source projects
Deep understanding of KV cache management, speculative decoding, and quantization
Experience with LLM evaluation frameworks
Hands-on experience with performance benchmarking and optimization
Deep understanding of Kubernetes
Familiarity with distributed serving architectures and autoscaling
Knowledge of InfiniBand, RoCE, or high-performance networking

Career growth and learning opportunities
Flexibility and ownership
Collaborative and innovative culture
Opportunity to work on impactful AI projects
International environment and talented teams

About Focused Energy
Focused Energy is a pioneering international deep-tech company with locations in Germany and the US, dedicated to commercializing laser-driven nuclear fusion. Our mission is to deliver clean, safe, and virtually limitless energy to the world. As we rapidly scale, we seek talented individuals who thrive on bringing clarity and structure to fast-growing environments.

As a Senior Software Engineer, you will be the primary software point of contact for the Laser team and provide technical leadership across software, hardware, and experimental-system interfaces. You will help define the architecture and technology direction for a greenfield laser-software platform while remaining hands-on in developing reliable tools for calibration, operation, human-machine interaction, and experimental data processing.
This role offers the opportunity to work across software, hardware, and experimental-system boundaries while contributing to a strong engineering culture within the Darmstadt Software Department. You will help shape technical direction, establish the foundations of a new software platform, and grow toward a broader technical leadership role. The position does not initially include direct people-management responsibility.

Act as the primary software partner for the Laser team and coordinate software activities across laser projects.
Provide technical leadership for software initiatives, including planning, technical alignment, risk identification, and coordination with laser physicists, engineers, and systems-integration partners.
Help define the architecture, technology choices, development practices, and interfaces for a new laser-software platform in a greenfield environment.
Design and implement reliable software for critical laser projects, from system-level interfaces to user-facing applications.
Develop and maintain automated calibration software that improves repeatability, reduces manual effort, and supports reliable laser operation.
Design and build clear, dependable human-machine interfaces, dashboards, and operational tools for monitoring and operating laser systems.
Develop software that interfaces with laser devices, diagnostic systems, cameras, and experimental equipment to support data acquisition, system monitoring, operational control, and visualization.
Develop data-processing pipelines and data-storage solutions for experimental and operational data, including diagnostic and camera data where appropriate.
Define robust interfaces between software, hardware, cameras, and experimental systems in an environment where requirements and technologies are still evolving.
Work with networked device and system interfaces, potentially including TCP/IP, REST APIs, webhooks, DDS, SCADA, or comparable communication technologies.
Write automated tests, technical documentation, and operational guidance to support long-term maintainability and safe, reliable operation.
Identify and address reliability, performance, integration, debugging, and maintenance risks in software that interacts with real-world systems.
Contribute to technical design discussions, code reviews, and knowledge sharing across the Software Department.
Mentor engineers and help establish engineering practices as the software team grows.

You are an experienced software engineer who enjoys solving complex, ambiguous technical problems and building systems from the ground up.
You are comfortable taking ownership of technical direction while collaborating closely with software specialists, laser physicists, experimental experts, and systems-integration partners.
You can move effectively between technical leadership, project coordination, architecture, and hands-on implementation.
You take ownership of the quality, reliability, testability, and long-term maintainability of the systems you build.
You communicate clearly with both software specialists and technical partners from adjacent disciplines.
You apply sound technical judgment when making design, implementation, and technology-selection decisions in an evolving environment.
You are curious, adaptable, and motivated to understand how software interacts with hardware, cameras, diagnostics, and experimental systems.
You are experienced in debugging and testing complex software and understand their importance in senior-level engineering work.
You value constructive feedback, knowledge sharing, and mentoring other engineers.
You are interested in developing toward technical leadership and project ownership. Formal people-management responsibility is not required at the outset.
Desirable Skills & Knowledge
Strong programming experience in C++, Python, or comparable programming languages.
Experience designing, implementing, testing, debugging, and maintaining complex software systems.
Knowledge of software architecture, code review practices, automated testing, technical documentation, and engineering best practices.
Experience with greenfield development, platform or architecture definition, and making technology choices where requirements are still evolving.
Experience with automated calibration, control-adjacent software, laboratory systems, automation, or physical-device interfaces.
Experience developing human-machine interfaces, dashboards, or software for operating technical equipment.
Experience with camera integration, image processing, diagnostic data, or experimental data-processing pipelines.

The mission of Speechify is to make sure that reading is never a barrier to learning.
Over 50 million people use Speechify’s text-to-speech products to turn whatever they’re reading – PDFs, books, Google Docs, news articles, websites – into audio, so they can read faster, read more, and remember more. Speechify’s text-to-speech reading products include its iOS app, Android App, Mac App, Chrome Extension, and Web App. Google recently named Speechify the Chrome Extension of the Year and Apple named Speechify its 2025 Design Award winner for Inclusivity.
Today, nearly 200 people around the globe work on Speechify in a 100% distributed setting – Speechify has no office.

The Platform team owns the backend behind everything Speechify ships: the public TTS API, payments, subscriptions, auth, consumption tracking, and analytics — serving over 50 million users across iOS, Android, Mac, Chrome, and web.
These are systems where correctness compounds. Subscription state has to stay consistent across five clients and two app-store billing systems that each go quiet at the worst moment. Consumption metering has to be exact enough to bill on and cheap enough to run at our request volume. The public TTS API has external customers with their own products depending on our latency and uptime. None of this degrades gracefully — it is either right, or someone gets charged twice.
The job is to make your own job smaller. Every system you own here should need less of you a year from now than it did the day you took it, and the reward for that is a larger one. That is the entire growth path on this team — there is no separate ladder, and no ceiling except the one you stop raising. We are a flat organization: people become leaders here by taking scope and being right about it, fast.
What Yo u’ ll Do
Design, build, and own the APIs behind payments, subscriptions, auth, consumption tracking, and our public TTS API
Take on services you didn't write and make them faster, cheaper, and harder to break
Establish that a change is correct before it ships, and leave behind the checks that keep it correct after you've moved on
Automate the parts of your role that shouldn't need a person, then go take on what that freed you up for
Turn work you've done once into work the whole team can repeat
Design B2B and enterprise integrations for customers building on top of us
Work with product, mobile, and web to keep backend architecture ahead of where the product is going

Proven backend experience in TS/Node (required)
Direct experience with GCP; working knowledge of AWS, Azure, or another cloud
A habit of giving away work you used to own, and something to show for the room it created
A daily working setup with AI agents you can describe in detail — what runs unattended, what you review, and where you've decided it doesn't get to act alone
The instinct to check a result against the system itself — logs, database state, the actual request — rather than against a summary of it
Judgment about what not to build, and the ability to say plainly why you dropped it
A preference for being corrected over being right
Preferred: deploying high-availability applications on Kubernetes

Several technical interviews plus a take-home assessment on a real codebase. We aim to finish within a week.
